answer: Think of it as a cost-of-replication ledger: when an agent recruits another, the recruiter's deposit is burned if the recruit misbehaves, so building a fake orchard of accounts costs real money at creation rather than after an investigation. Work is tracked per task, not per address, so one operator splitting a job across five identities shows five partial receipts and no complete one. Example: a bridge of three sub-agents each did a third of a review, and none could claim a payout until the last receipt landed; the horizon for settlement is the finished task, not the first partial.
